_comment: Example `<repo_root>/.crustify/build.json` (REPO-ROOT tier) emitted by CrustifyBuildPropose. Captures build-system metadata downstream consumers (composer modules, file_mapper, CrustifyBuildExecute) treat as authoritative for library partitioning, link topology, feature gating, and build invocation. Lives at the repo-root tier because it describes the whole repository's build, independent of any specific target subdirectory crustify is scoped to. All paths inside this file are repo-root-relative. Values below are an OpenSSL libssl example; substitute for other projects. After the agent emits this file, the user is expected to review and approve before downstream stages run.
_comment_libraries: Per-library descriptors keyed by library name. **The key MUST be the stem of `target`** - the filename without path or extension. `libssl.so` -> key `libssl`; `providers/fips.so` -> key `fips`; `libcrypto.a` -> key `libcrypto`. System libraries (no `target`) use their conventional short name: `libc`, `libm`, `libpthread`. This naming rule guarantees consistency with the actual on-disk artifacts the linker produces, which is what downstream link-time attribution (a future symtab-resolution stage) will match against. `kind` is `shared` / `static` / `system`. `target` is the build output filename for shared/static; `null` for system. `source_dirs` are directories whose source files (.c / .cc / .cpp) compile into this library's target. `include_dirs` are directories where this library's header files live; **these MAY overlap between libraries** (e.g. OpenSSL's `include/openssl/` is in both libssl and libcrypto). Headers are NOT enumerated here - file-to-library attribution happens at file_mapper time. `link_dependencies` lists the OTHER libraries this one links against; each entry must reference a library you also define here.
_comment_executables: Binary executable targets and their link-time library dependencies. Informational - composer uses this to identify executable-only files (e.g. OpenSSL's `apps/`) that aren't library-bound and may fall in `config.json.out_of_scope`. Each `link_dependencies` entry must reference a library defined in `libraries` above.
_comment_features: All compile-time features the build system exposes, documented as a flat list under `features.all`. Each entry is a record with four fields: **name** is the feature macro the project's source code keys on (e.g. `OPENSSL_THREADS`, `OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_3_0`, `OPENSSL_USE_NODELETE`). **role** is a free-form explanation of what the feature does + its lifecycle status (deprecated/legacy/transitional/stable/transitional) - **cite the documentation source** that informs the description (`per CHANGES.md`, `per Configure line 1792`, `per INSTALL.md`, etc.); generic descriptions without sourcing aren't useful to downstream consumers. **default_value** is the value the feature takes when the project's standard configure step runs without flags. **enabled** is what this build's specific configure invocation produces - initially the same as `default_value`; downstream consumers (the user, the orchestrator, future configure-specific stages) override based on the actual `build_commands.configure` flag set. The composer unions `{name | features.all[i].enabled = false}` with `config.json.out_of_scope.features` to compute the effective disabled-feature set for filtering dead code. There is no separate top-level `enabled` / `disabled` / `legacy` partition - the `enabled` boolean per feature gives current build state; the `role` field gives roadmap status.

all.name: OPENSSL_THREADS
all.role: Enables POSIX threading support for thread-safe global state and per-context locks. Per INSTALL.md and Configure script defaults, automatically defined on all POSIX builds.

all.name: OPENSSL_USE_NODELETE
all.role: Marks the shared library as RTLD_NODELETE - never unmapped, even when dlclose'd. Per Configure script defaults, enabled on shared Linux builds to support thread-local state safely.

all.name: OPENSSL_PIC
all.role: Generates position-independent code (-fPIC); required for shared libraries on most platforms. Per Configure script, set automatically when building shared libraries.

all.name: OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_3_0
all.role: Disables APIs deprecated in OpenSSL 3.0 (RSA low-level, ENGINE, EVP low-level, SRP, OCSP_REQ_CTX, ...). Per CHANGES.md, scheduled for removal. Defining excludes these surfaces from compilation. Legacy / transitional.

all.name: OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_3_5
all.role: Disables APIs deprecated in OpenSSL 3.5. Per CHANGES.md, a continuation of the deprecation wave from 3.0. Legacy / transitional.

all.name: OPENSSL_NO_ASM
all.role: Disables hand-written assembly optimisations across crypto primitives; forces the C reference implementations. Per Configure script, can be set via `no-asm`. Performance vs portability trade-off; sometimes required for unusual targets or sanitizer builds.

all.name: OPENSSL_LEGACY_PROVIDER
all.role: Documented in doc/man7/migration_guide.pod as the transitional provider hosting pre-3.0 algorithms (MD2, MD4, MDC2, RC4, DES, ...). Loaded via OSSL_PROVIDER_load but not part of the default crypto path. Legacy / transitional.

_comment_build_commands: Shell commands `CrustifyBuildExecute` invokes to set up the build under CodeQL trace. Each is a shell-quoted string executed in the `target` working directory. `configure` and `build` are REQUIRED. `test` and `clean` are optional but recommended. The executor wraps `build` with the CodeQL trace command; `configure` runs uninstrumented. Quote literal values containing shell metacharacters with single quotes inside the string.
